detailed_description:
Preserve the source scene's visual treatment while retaining the replacement character's distinctive design. Adapt illumination, shading, and perspective to the source scene.

[Shot 1] (0.0 to 3.5 seconds) A wide, static shot of the living room. <Subject 1> starts on the grey sofa, walks along the cushions, leaps off the armrest onto the wooden bookshelf, and walks along the top of the shelf toward the window, pausing to look around.

Follow <Video 1> exactly: every shot, cut, camera move, action and its timing. Match the original performance moment by moment: posture, steps, gestures, head turns, gaze, expressions and timing.

Maintain each reference character's identity through every expression and viewing angle. Hair and clothing move naturally with the transferred performance. Preserve interactions with source-scene objects and the ordering of foreground and background occlusions.

Keep the source video's crop and shot scale. Show only the portions of the replacement characters that belong within that framing; do not widen the shot to reproduce the full-body reference. Do not import the reference images' backgrounds, static poses, or handheld props. Preserve the source camera movement and action timing through the final frame.

overall_soundscape:

non_diegetic_music:
